newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, China plan to set up joint cargo airline.
newsitem.headline: Russia, China plan to set up joint cargo airline.

text.p: Russia and China plan to set up a new joint cargo airline, aviation officials said on Thursday.
A spokesman for Russia's Transport Ministry said Minister Nikolai Tsakh planned an official visit to China on April 28 to discuss the project.
Yakov Serov said leading Russian cargo carrier Volga-Dnepr was interested in taking part in the project.

"We have a big interest in establishing the joint airline because it will allow us to expand Volga-Dnepr cargo operations into the Chinese market, which is very promising," Volga-Dnepr spokesman Konstantin Rogov said. "We think it will be a joint venture with China's State Aviation Corporation."
Itar-Tass news agency said China's State Aviation Corporation operated six Yakovlev Yak-42 jets and owned an international airport in China.
Volga-Dnepr chief executive Alexei Isaykin plans to travel to China with the delegation headed by the transport minister, Rogov said.

Volga-Dnepr makes scheduled cargo flights from Ulyanovsk in central Russia to three destinations in China, operating heavy cargo jets Antonov An-124s and Ilyushin Il-76s. They carry mostly consumer goods and home electronics to Russia as well as heavy machinery to China.

Rogov said the company's 1996 sales volume on flights to and from China was $11.7 million, compared with $10 million in the previous year. The airline expected $20 million sales volume on these routes in this year, Rogov added.
Its total sales volume was fixed at $111 million last year compared with $82 million in 1995.

Last year, Volga-Dnepr carried a total of 45,000 tonnes of cargo or 13 per cent of Russia's total air cargo turnover, second to Aeroflot, which carried 89,500 tonnes or 26 per cent of total cargo turnover.
